sections.label: Planning estimate
items: This course's estimate: `tokens ≈ characters / 4` for English text.
Real tokenizers vary by provider and are more precise, use this for planning only.

sections.label: Chunking rules
items: Never silently drop content: an oversized single word still gets its own chunk, even if it alone exceeds the budget.
Overlap repeats boundary content so no idea is split with zero context on either side, typically 10–20% of chunk size.
More overlap = more total tokens processed = more cost, it's a tradeoff, not a free win.

sections.label: The oversized-word guard
sections.formula: if tokens + t > max and len(chunk) > 0: break  # only enforce once chunk is non-empty

sections.label: Common mistakes
items: Truncating instead of chunking: silently drops whatever came after the cut, with no error.
Enforcing the budget check even on an empty chunk, silently dropping an oversized single word.
Forgetting that a retry re-sends the ENTIRE original prompt plus new context, roughly doubling token cost.

sections.label: Implementation checklist
checklist: Available input budget is computed, not assumed.
Chunker never drops a word, oversized or not.
Overlap is applied consistently at every chunk boundary except the last.
